title: Projection base change at rational coefficients
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, an integer $n\ge1$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ containing $E$. Let $S$ be a six-functor datum at these coefficients [def-sf-datum], with the specified operation and comparison data [def-fix-six-functor-datum].

Work at $\Lambda=E$ in the raw rationalized integral categories $D^b_c(T,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].

Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{array}$$
be a Cartesian square of finite-type $k$-schemes. Assume $f$ is separated, and supply a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ with $j$ open, $p$ proper and $pj=f$, together with its Cartesian base change $c'=(j',p')$; all squares and factorizations are part of the specified compactified square. No separatedness of $g$ or of the structure morphisms is assumed. Write $U_u=Lu^*$, $F=Rf_!^c$, $F'=Rf'_!^{c'}$, and $P_f(K,L)=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^c$, using the datum's recorded projection components [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates, def-exchange-projection]. Let $e_M:U_gFM\to F'U_{g'}M$ be the specified compact-support exchange, with only the datum's endpoint identifications. Let $\mu_u(A,B):U_u(A\otimes B)\xrightarrow{\sim}U_uA\otimes U_uB$ be the canonical normalized tensor-pullback comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison], and let $\kappa_L:U_{g'}U_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{f'}U_gL$ be the inverse pullback compositor to $U_{fg'}L$, transport through $fg'=gf'$, then the pullback compositor to $U_{f'}U_gL$. Tensor and pullback at $R$ are completed, at $E$ rationalized, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ represented over a common finite field. For the inputs specified below, the following equality holds:
$$\begin{aligned}
F'\bigl((1\otimes\kappa_L)\circ\mu_{g'}(K,U_fL)\bigr)\circ e_{K\otimes U_fL}\circ U_g(P_f(K,L))
={}&P_{f'}(U_{g'}K,U_gL)\circ(e_K\otimes1)\circ\mu_g(FK,L).
\end{aligned}$$
Both sides have source $U_g(FK\otimes L)$ and target $F'(U_{g'}K\otimes U_{f'}U_gL)$, using exactly the specified maps, rather than independently chosen isomorphisms.

Here $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ are arbitrary; no extra second-input Tor hypothesis is imposed.

Verbatim retained old parent argument, in source order:
Choose $f=pj$ and its Cartesian base change; by [def-exchange-projection] $\operatorname{PF}^c=R(\gamma_j)\pi_p$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=R'(\beta)e$. Apply [lem-sf-pf-open-base-change-square] with $M=j_!K$, $Q=M\otimes FL$: it supplies all completed constructible domains, monoidality of $\theta:F'G\cong HF$, and the open-factor equality. The ordinary adjunctions are [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). The proper exchange $e$ is their specified mate of $\theta$ by [def-exchange-projection, fix-lem-exchanges], and $\pi_p$ is the counit projection. Apply [lem-sp-categorical-projection-mate-square] with its adjunctions $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$, $Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$, $N_D=G$, $N_C=H$, $\alpha=\theta$, $\varphi=\mu_F$, $\varphi'=\mu_{F'}$, $m_C=\mu_H$, $m_D=\mu_G$; its hypothesis ComparisonCompatible is the monoidality equation just cited. Its conclusion is $R'(d)e_QG(\pi_{p;M,L})=\pi_{p';HM,GL}(e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;RM,L}$ with $d=(1\otimes\theta_L^{-1})\mu_H$, the proper-factor hypothesis of [lem-sf-pf-compactification-pasting]; the open one is the equality above. That pasting identity gives the displayed square: its target comparison is $La^*JFL\cong J'HFL\to J'F'GL\cong Lf'^*GL$. Refinement compatibility and square naturality in [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(4), with projection compatibility from step 1, remove the compactification choice; the naturality clause of the pasting lemma gives naturality in the morphism data. At finite coefficients apply [lem-sf-finite-base-change-transport]: its proof identifies each constructible-coordinate route under faithful realization, substitutes the existing fixed-scalar diamond equality, cancels the common target isomorphism, and reflects equality through the full inclusion. This retains the proper/open mate calculation and adds no separatedness of the horizontal map.

Exact sorried source theorem header:
theorem sixFunctorProjection_baseChange_rational (S : SixFunctorDatum D C E n hn) :
    ∀ (Q : SixFunctorCompactifiedSquare D)
      [IsSeparated Q.f.hom.left]
      (K : sfRationalConstructibleCategory C.l E Q.X.obj.left)
      (L : sfRationalConstructibleCategory C.l E Q.Y.obj.left),
      (S.higher.rational.pull Q.g).map ((S.higher.rationalExchange Q).projectionComponent K L) ≫
        sixFunctorProjectionExchange (S.higher.rationalExchange Q)
          (((S.higher.rationalTensor Q.X).obj K).obj ((S.higher.rational.pull Q.f).obj L)) ≫
        (S.higher.rational.support Q.f' Q.compactification').map
          ((sixFunctorProjectionRationalMu S Q.g' K
            ((S.higher.rational.pull Q.f).obj L)).hom ≫
            ((S.higher.rationalTensor Q.X').obj ((S.higher.rational.pull Q.g').obj K)).map
              (((S.higher.rational.pullComposition Q.g' Q.f).inv.app L) ≫
                eqToHom (congrArg
                  (fun f ↦ (S.higher.rational.pull f).obj L) Q.squareComm) ≫
                (S.higher.rational.pullComposition Q.f' Q.g).hom.app L)) =
      (sixFunctorProjectionRationalMu S Q.g
        ((S.higher.rational.support Q.f Q.compactification).obj K) L).hom ≫
        ((S.higher.rationalTensor Q.Y').map
          (sixFunctorProjectionExchange (S.higher.rationalExchange Q) K)).app
            ((S.higher.rational.pull Q.g).obj L) ≫
        (S.higher.rationalExchange (compactSupportProjectionSquare Q.f'
          Q.compactification')).projectionComponent
          ((S.higher.rational.pull Q.g').obj K) ((S.higher.rational.pull Q.g).obj L)

proof.text: Let $Q_T:D^b_c(T,R)\to D^b_c(T,E)$ be raw scalar localization. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] its objects are unchanged, so the given $K,L$ have integral objects $K_0,L_0$ with $Q_XK_0=K$, $Q_YL_0=L$; no lattice-existence or idempotent-splitting assertion is needed. Apply [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] to $L_0$ on $Y$: the coefficient datum is the same, $L_0$ is derived-complete bounded constructible, and $\ell\ne p$. Its conclusion gives the uniform finite-reduction Tor interval required by the integral base-change statement. There is no corresponding restriction to check on $K_0$.

proof.text: Use precisely the supplied compactified Cartesian square, unchanged over $R$, and apply [lem-sf-projection-base-change-integral] to $K_0,L_0$. Its hypotheses require separatedness only of $f$ and the uniform Tor condition established in step 1; they permit the given arbitrary $g$ and nonseparated structure morphisms. Denote its left and right composites by $A_0,B_0$. It gives $A_0=B_0$ in the completed integral category on $Y'$, with the specified projection, exchange, tensor-pullback comparison and inverse/composite pullback comparison. This is an integral arrow equality, not an inference from its finite evaluations; the existing integral node carries the unit's open-factor, proper-mate and pasting calculation.

source.place: Base-change paragraph, open/proper factor and pasting calculation, supplied by the existing integral-stage node

proof.text: Identify the primitive maps under $Q_T$ before comparing composites. By [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] the rational pullback, tensor and compact-support functors are the integral operations on objects of the raw localization, with morphisms tensored with $E$; by [lem-fix-operation-reduction] rationalization commutes with these operations and with ordinary direct image, preserving the units, counits and tensor associativity maps constructing projection and exchange. Hence the comparisons $Q_VLu^*\cong Lu^*Q_W$, $Q_WRu_*\cong Ru_*Q_V$, $Q_Wj_!\cong j_!Q_V$ and $Q_W(M\otimes N)\cong Q_WM\otimes Q_WN$ are these canonical identifications, and their identity and composition cocycles hold. The (A5) clause of [def-sf-datum] refers to the coefficient comparison data of [def-exchange-projection], which states that at the rational stage the adjunction units and counits, the pullback-composition and tensor-pullback isomorphisms and the open-immersion maps $\beta,\gamma$ are the rationalizations of the integral maps; for the canonical $\mu_u$ used here, [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison] likewise defines its rational hom and inverse as the localizations of the integral ones. Thus the comparisons meet the primitive-map intertwining hypotheses of [lem-sf-pf-coefficient-realization-transport], for $T_T=Q_T$ on the displayed bounded integral domains. That lemma identifies the images of $\pi_p,e_p,\operatorname{PF}^c,\operatorname{Ex}_!^c$ and their whiskered base-change routes with the specified rational maps. It uses the same $c,c'$ and the datum's endpoint comparisons; it chooses no new exchange isomorphism.

source.place: Rational specialization: primitive-map normalization and comparison-functor transport of the two base-change routes

proof.text: Write $A_E,B_E$ for the two composites in the statement. With $s_0,t_0$ the common endpoints of $A_0,B_0$, let $c_s:Q_{Y'}s_0\xrightarrow{\sim}s_E$ and $c_t:Q_{Y'}t_0\xrightarrow{\sim}t_E$ be the composite endpoint comparisons of step 3. The transport lemma gives $c_tQ_{Y'}(A_0)=A_Ec_s$ and $c_tQ_{Y'}(B_0)=B_Ec_s$. Functoriality applied to step 2 and cancellation of $c_s$ give $A_E=B_E$. In the target comparison $\kappa_L$, localization sends the inverse integral compositor to its inverse (apply the functor to both inverse identities), sends the square-equality transport to the same transport, and sends the final compositor to the recorded one; hence the target is exactly $F'(U_{g'}K\otimes U_{f'}U_gL)$. The rational category has no extra objects by step 1, so this proves the assertion for all given $K,L$, without adding a Tor condition or reducing a field-coefficient object.
